The action declares only 204 and 404 (`[ProducesResponseType(Status204NoContent)]`, `Status404NotFound`) and the vendored contract declares no 500 for this path, so the throw is unintended, not a documented behaviour — Ferrofin's `FerrofinTaskManager::stop_run` returns Ok for an already-idle task (404 only for an unknown id) and is kept correct (do not port Jellyfin bugs). MEASURED 2026-08-30 on the loop pair, deterministic, not a race: POST-then-DELETE on `ec2f221fd8e7706b3d3afd2c4591b4d7` (Audio Normalization) is (204, 500) four times running on Jellyfin and (204, 204) four times on Ferrofin, and a DELETE with nothing running at all is 500 vs 204. The journeys row therefore reads H=True J=False and only goes red on a WARM lab: the first Audio Normalization run does real work and is still Running when the DELETE lands (which is why an earlier journeys record has it green), while every later run finishes in well under a millisecond. Seeds of this kind take the C# FLAT provider: one `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [<kind>], EnableGroupByMetadataKey = false, EnableTotalRecordCount = true, OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, SortOrder.Ascending)] }` — identical in v10.11.8 (built inline at LibraryController.cs:791-801) and in master (SeriesSimilarItemsProvider.cs:49, MusicAlbumSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, AudioSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, LiveTvProgramSimilarItemsProvider.cs:89). Ferrofin runs the same query and, as of this pass, the same `Random` order. IT BRIEFLY DID NOT: batch A2 first shipped `SortName` here, which is not cosmetic — at limit < |candidates| a fixed order returns a DIFFERENT ITEM, measured on the loop pair as `/Items/{audio}/Similar?limit=1` answering 'Artist 01 Album 01 Track 02' on five consecutive Ferrofin calls while Jellyfin alternated Track 02 / Track 03. That divergence is now closed in the server (`similar_items_manager.rs::flat_similar`, unit test `the_flat_provider_orders_random_not_by_name`), not papered over. The reads.py leg therefore pins `limit=1000`, far above the fixture's pool, where the answer is the whole candidate set and so fully determined; what is gated there is the SET, TotalRecordCount and every per-item DTO field. Anything order-sensitive is covered by unit tests instead, never by this row. GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): Ferrofin returns 0 rows where Jellyfin returns 2. What still blocks it is the item-UNIVERSE divergence, not the similarity code: Ferrofin materializes MusicArtist as a parentless by-name row with a NULL TopParentId, and every user-scoped `InternalItemsQuery` is scoped to the user's views via `TopParentId IS NOT NULL` (item_repository.rs `scope_to_user_libraries`, the port of C# `AddUserToQuery`), so no artist is reachable by any query that does not name it by id. Detector, both servers: `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=MusicArtist` -> F 0, J 3, while `/Artists?userId=<u>` returns all 3 on both, and adding `&ids=<artistId>` makes the same query return the row on Ferrofin. Same root cause as the MusicArtist/Folder/TvChannel/UserView rows missing from GET /Items/Suggestions. Un-defer path: give the MusicArtist by-name row a TopParentId (Jellyfin's artist rows are physical folder items under the music library, which is why they survive `AddUserToQuery`) — this changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it needs its own change with the perf gate, not a ride-along. GET /Items/Suggestions.classification: open-work (NOT accepted). The old text ('Random, so the set is non-deterministic') was only half true and it hid two real divergences. Random here PERMUTES but does not change the set: `SuggestionsController` runs ONE query (`OrderBy = [(Random, Descending)]`, Recursive, mediaType/type, IsVirtualItem=false) and Ferrofin's handler is a line-for-line port, so at `limit >= |universe|` the answer is fully determined and parity_diff aligns Items by Path. The probe was the problem: `limit=10` sampled 10 of 552 at random and could never diff. It is now eight legs: seven pinned at a full limit (per type), where Random only permutes and the whole body IS diffed, plus one narrow startIndex/limit leg. That narrow leg is the one place a projection is applied — a page of 3 out of 500 Random-ordered rows draws a different triple per call on BOTH servers (measured: three consecutive calls, three different triples each side), so it compares StartIndex, TotalRecordCount and the page length only. Diffing its Items would pin this row red forever and destroy its ability to signal when the two real divergences below are fixed; the projection is scoped to that leg alone and nothing was added to parity_diff.VOLATILE. Two causes remain, BOTH owned by other rows and deliberately left visible here rather than filtered out of the probe: (1) ITEM UNIVERSE — Ferrofin's recursive user-root universe has no MusicArtist, Folder, TvChannel or UserView rows (F 552 vs J 561 unfiltered; per type F 0 vs J 3/3/2/1), the same parentless-by-name/TopParentId cause as GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar; detector `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&limit=100000`, which shows the identical 9-row delta, so it is not this handler's bug. (2) PER-ITEM DTO FIELDS — MediaSources[].Name/Bitrate, MediaStreams[].BitRate (a constant 192000 offset), LocalizedLanguage, Level/IsAVC/Width/Height: the same set already classified on GET /Items/{itemId} as independent-probe noise, inherited here because Suggestions returns full item DTOs. Narrowing the compare to hide either would be the dishonest green; the row stays red until they are fixed on their own rows. The multi-leg probe no longer skips a leg whose servers disagree on status: a status divergence (or a body that is not 200-with-JSON on both sides) is recorded as a mismatch, which is the whole point of keeping the type=MusicArtist and type=TvChannel legs. UNIVERSE GAP, re-measured 2026-08-29 and WIDER than first written: LiveTvProgram belongs on the missing-kind list too — `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=LiveTvProgram` returns 338 rows on Jellyfin and 0 on Ferrofin, while `/LiveTv/Programs` returns the guide on both (F 19200, J 338). The knock-on is visible on a THIRD row: GET /Genres is red only because Jellyfin's genre list carries `News`, the XMLTV guide's programme genre, which Ferrofin's genre list cannot see for the same reason. One fix (give the by-name/programme rows a TopParentId so `scope_to_user_libraries` stops filtering them out) closes /Artists Similar, these Suggestions legs and the /Genres row together; it changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it is its own change WITH the perf gate.

GET /Items/{itemId}.classification: jellyfin-bug, on TWO independent fields. (1) BITRATE. Ferrofin reports MediaStreams[video].BitRate as container-minus-other-streams and MediaSources[].Bitrate as the stream sum; Jellyfin 10.11.8 falls the video stream back to formatInfo.BitRate verbatim (v10.11.8 ProbeResultNormalizer.cs:978-987) and then InferTotalBitrate(true) (PRN.cs:259-264), which double-counts the audio. Measured on the fixture: the file is 775053 B / 1.023 s = 6,060,832 bps, so Jellyfin's MediaSources[].Bitrate of 6,253,020 exceeds what the file physically contains, while Ferrofin's 6,061,020 matches ffprobe's own format.bit_rate. Upstream fixed this itself in PR #16248 (master PRN.cs:979-991 comments that formatInfo.BitRate is the container, not the video bitrate) and Ferrofin ports the fixed form. (2) PROBE-DTO NULLABILITY (Level / IsAVC / Width / Height). Upstream MASTER declares all four nullable — MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Probing/MediaStreamInfo.cs:93 `public int? Width`, :107 `public int? Height`, :170 `public int? Level`, :233 `public bool? IsAvc` — so a stream for which ffprobe emits no such key keeps null. v10.11.8 declares the same four as non-nullable value types at the same file's :95 `public int Width`, :109 `public int Height`, :172 `public int Level`, :235 `public bool IsAvc`, so an absent key deserializes to the CLR default and 10.11.8 then emits `Level: 0` and `IsAVC: false` on EVERY stream — audio and subtitle included, where neither value is meaningful — plus `Width: 0`/`Height: 0` on a text subtitle. Ferrofin ports MASTER and is correct. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-30 on the loop pair, GET /Items/{id}?fields=MediaSources,MediaStreams and POST /Items/{id}/PlaybackInfo, item d37ecb9d75b0c0a8e9ecb0a864ec670e (Movie 0001), after re-probing all 500 correlated movies on Ferrofin: video stream identical on both (Level 12, IsAVC true, 320x240); audio stream J=`Level:0, IsAVC:false` vs H=both keys ABSENT; subrip subtitle J=`Level:0, IsAVC:false, Width:0, Height:0` vs H=all four keys ABSENT. *** CORRECTION TO BATCH A3 (this entry supersedes it). A3 (commit e4f1b37) read the four fields off v10.11.8 only, called Ferrofin's nullable form a bug, and changed both the probing DTO and ProbeResultNormalizer to fabricate 0/false. That was a REGRESSION against the project rule that the WIRE CONTRACT is pinned to 10.11.8 while the BEHAVIOUR Ferrofin ports is upstream master, and it was reverted in batch M1 (probing/dtos.rs back to Option<i32>/Option<bool>; probe_result_normalizer.rs back to master's shape — Width/Height/Level in the shared initializer at master PRN.cs:702-714, IsAVC in the video arm only at master PRN.cs:794). The diff above is the expected consequence and is NOT a reason to change Ferrofin back, and NOT a reason to widen parity_diff.VOLATILE. A3's OTHER probing change is CORRECT and stands: codec_tag_string binds the plain JSON key (v10.11.8 MediaStreamInfo.cs:206), because the trailing-`?` typo is a master-only regression (master :204) that stops the key deserializing at all. *** OWNER CALL PENDING on the bitrate arithmetic: porting 10.11.8's instead would make this row body-diffable at the cost of being wrong. OPEN QUESTION, NOT AN AGENT DECISION — MediaStream.LocalizedLanguage: upstream master populates it for audio and subtitle streams (master ProbeResultNormalizer.cs:781 in the subtitle arm and the matching audio arm), but the vendored 10.11.8 OpenAPI declares MediaStream with `additionalProperties: false`, so emitting it makes every body carrying a language-tagged stream schema_valid:false. A3 withheld it from the wire; batch M1 deliberately left that as-is pending the owner's answer. The two halves are: master emits the field; the pinned contract forbids it. Whoever answers, record the decision here and either serialize the field or state why the contract wins. NOTE: the 'instance/probe-noise' text this row carried before A3 was DISPROVEN — running both containers' ffprobe binaries over the same file gives byte-identical JSON (7.1.4 vs 7.1.3-Jellyfin), and ffprobe emits no per-stream bit_rate at all. A3's other real fixes stand: MediaSources[].Name ports BaseItem.GetMediaSourceName (file stem, not item.Name), and the People[].Role read projection no longer NULLIFs the empty string C# always emits. LAB-STATE RECORD, so it is not lost (batch M1): the re-probe M1 needed in order to see the code change at all (the four values are PERSISTED at probe time, so a container rebuild alone changes nothing) also cleared a set of TMDB-scraped fields Ferrofin was carrying on the five correlated movies and Jellyfin was not. The pre-M1 run recorded them as Ferrofin extras — CommunityRating, OfficialRating, OriginalTitle, Overview, PremiereDate, ProviderIds.Tmdb, ExternalUrls[Name=TMDB], plus Taglines[] (J len 0, H len 1) and PrimaryImageAspectRatio. They did NOT come back on a second `metadataRefreshMode=FullRefresh&replaceAllMetadata=true`, so the remote fetch is not reachable/enabled in this lab today and those values were one-time state from an earlier lab epoch, not a reproducible server divergence. TODO (un-defer path, NOT accepted): re-run this row on a lab where the TMDB fetcher is reachable and either reproduce the extras — in which case the real question is why Jellyfin's fetch does not populate the same fields off the same `uniqueid type=imdb tt0111161` in the fixture movie.nfo — or confirm the fields are gone for good.

GET /System/Logs.classification: instance: `LogFile` has four fields and two (DateCreated/DateModified) are already VOLATILE, so a diff could only compare Name and Size — and both are the host's own. Jellyfin's Serilog sink writes `log_YYYYMMDD.log` (Jellyfin.Server/Resources/Configuration/logging.json: `%JELLYFIN_LOG_DIR%//log_.log`, rollingInterval Day) while Ferrofin's tracing-appender writes `log.YYYY-MM-DD.log` (apps/ferrofin-server/src/bootstrap.rs); Size is each server's own log volume. Name is also parity_diff's array-align key, so the sweep can only ever report '(whole item)'. Body-diff is structurally impossible; the row is earned as `property` by assets.py. It was. `TranscodeManager.StartFfMpeg` (MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Transcoding/TranscodeManager.cs:450-467 at v10.11.8) writes each transcode's ffmpeg stderr into `ApplicationPaths.LogDirectoryPath` as `FFmpeg.Transcode-`/`FFmpeg.Remux-`/`FFmpeg.DirectStream-{yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss}_{mediaSourceId}_{guid8}.log` — deliberately into the directory this route serves ('let's put it in the log directory'), so an operator can download a failed transcode's log from the dashboard. Ferrofin wrote it beside the playlist in the transcode temp dir instead (`playlist_path.with_extension("log")`), so its listing held no ffmpeg log at all while Jellyfin's held several. FIXED IN THE SERVER: `StartFfMpegRequest` now carries the LOG DIRECTORY and `TranscodeManagerImpl::start_ffmpeg` names the file with the ported `ffmpeg_log_file_name`. assets.py starts a real transcode on each server and then asserts the listing contains a matching name — a fact both servers must satisfy, and the one a Name/Size diff could never reach. The rest of the row is unchanged: the exact 4-key `LogFile` contract, the .txt/.log extension filter (`ManagedFileSystem.GetFiles` — the Jellyfin container's extension-less `.jellyfin-log` must be absent), bare filenames, and the C# ordering rule OrderByDescending(DateModified).ThenByDescending(DateCreated).ThenBy(Name), unit-tested in crates/ferrofin-api/tests/system.rs. `sig_match` now fails this row when either server answers False on any of those facts, or when the fact could not be established at all — agreeing on a broken invariant is not parity.

POST /Packages/Installed/{name}.classification: accepted-divergence: repository install of WASM plugins is real (2026-08-14: ABI gate → HTTPS-per-hop download → streamed size cap → sha256/md5 verify → component+identity validation → guid-squat refusal → atomic stage → restart-required; admin-only; end-to-end server test). Async install + Package* push is the recorded follow-up (WebSocket-push backlog).
